item.subject: Mathematics
item.stem:
There are several ways of arranging the tiles so that they form patterns. The grid below has been shaded to show how tiles can be placed on some of the squares. The pattern can be continued so that AB and CD are lines of symmetry.

[Image: A 4 by 4 grid with symmetry axes AB and CD]

Shade in all the remaining squares on the grid so that the resulting pattern is symmetrical about line AB, and also is symmetrical about line CD.

descriptors: Both quadrants correctly shaded (pattern shaded or demarcated in some way making symmetrical pattern about both axes, AB and CD).
One of the two quadrants correctly shaded.
Incorrect (including crossed out/erased, stray marks, illegible, or off task).

item.figure_description:
A 4-by-4 square grid of 16 unit squares, divided into four 2-by-2 quadrants by a vertical line AB (with A at the top, B at the bottom) and a horizontal line CD (with C at the left, D at the right).
Two quadrants are shaded with tile patterns:
- Top-right 2-by-2 quadrant (rows 1-2, columns 3-4):
  - Row 1, column 3: small black square in the top-left corner.
  - Row 1, column 4: small black square in the top-right corner.
  - Row 2, column 3: small black square in the bottom-left corner.
  - Row 2, column 4: small black square in the bottom-right corner.
  - In the center of this 2-by-2 quadrant (where the four squares meet), a large black diamond (rotated square) is formed across the inner corners of all four squares.
- Bottom-left 2-by-2 quadrant (rows 3-4, columns 1-2):
  - Shaded with the exact same pattern: four small black corner squares at the outer corners of the 2-by-2 quadrant, and a large black diamond centered where the four squares meet.
The top-left 2-by-2 quadrant and bottom-right 2-by-2 quadrant are entirely blank (unshaded).
item.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1999 and 2003 eighth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
Pat has red tiles and black tiles. Pat uses the tiles to make square shapes.

The 3 × 3 shape has 1 black tile and 8 red tiles.
[Image: A black tile in the middle, surrounded by the 8 red tiles, to make a square shape.]

The 4 × 4 shape has 4 black tiles and 12 red tiles.
[Image: Four black tiles forming a square in the center, with 12 red tiles lining the sides, to create a larger square shape.]

The table below shows the number of tiles for the first three shapes Pat made. Pat continued making shapes using this pattern. Complete the table for the 6 × 6 and 7 × 7 shapes.

| Shape | Number of Black Tiles | Number of Red Tiles | Total Number of Tiles |
| :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: |
| 3 × 3 | 1 | 8 | 9 |
| 4 × 4 | 4 | 12 | 16 |
| 5 × 5 | 9 | 16 | 25 |
| 6 × 6 | 16 | | |
| 7 × 7 | 25 | | |

descriptors:
Both rows completely correct
Shape 6 x 6: 20, 36
Shape 7 x 7: 24, 49
Entries for one row correct but not both

Entries for one column correct but not both
Red Tiles: 20, 24   OR   Total Tiles: 36, 49
Other incorrect (including crossed out, erased, stray marks, illegible, or off task)

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
A half-turn about point P in the plane is applied to the shaded figure.

[Image: Shaded figure on dashed axes]

Which of the following shows the results of the half-turn?

options.label: A
options.text: [Image: Shaded right triangle above the horizontal line with vertical side on the left]

options.label: B
options.text: [Image: Shaded right triangle below the horizontal line with vertical side on the right]

options.label: C
options.text: [Image: Shaded right triangle above the horizontal line with vertical side on the right]

options.label: D
options.text: [Image: Shaded right triangle below the horizontal line with vertical side on the left]

options.label: E
options.text: [Image: Shaded right triangle below the horizontal line with rightmost vertex at point P]

reference_items.figure_description:
In the stem diagram, a horizontal dashed line and a vertical dashed line intersect perpendicularly at point P, which is marked with a black dot and labeled P below the horizontal line. A shaded right triangle lies above the horizontal dashed line. Its bottom horizontal base lies along the horizontal dashed line, extending both to the left and to the right of point P, with the segment to the left of P being longer than the segment to the right of P. The right edge of the triangle is vertical, extending upward from the horizontal line. The hypotenuse connects the top-right vertex to the leftmost vertex on the horizontal dashed line. The vertical dashed line passes through the shaded triangle.

Option A shows a shaded right triangle above the horizontal line, with its base on the horizontal line extending to both sides of P (longer to the right of P), its vertical side on the left extending upward, and hypotenuse sloping down to the right.
Option B shows a shaded right triangle below the horizontal line, with its base on the horizontal line extending to both sides of P (longer to the left of P), its vertical side on the right extending downward, and hypotenuse sloping up to the left.
Option C shows a shaded right triangle above the horizontal line, with its base on the horizontal line, vertical side on the right extending upward, and hypotenuse sloping down to the left.
Option D shows a shaded right triangle below the horizontal line, with its base on the horizontal line extending to both sides of P (longer to the right of P), its vertical side on the left extending downward, and hypotenuse sloping up to the right.
Option E shows a shaded right triangle below the horizontal line, with its base on the horizontal line located entirely to the left of point P, touching point P at its rightmost acute vertex, with its vertical side on the left extending downward.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2003 data, 2007 bridging data, and 2007 data (eighth-grade mathematics).

reference_items.stem:
Pat wanted to add a line to the table showing how to find the number of tiles needed to make a square of any size. Use the patterns in the table on the opposite page to help you complete the line for shape n × n in the table below.

| Shape | Number of Black Tiles | Number of Red Tiles | Total Number of Tiles |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| n × n | (n − 2)^2 | | |

descriptors:
Both expressions correct in simplified form
Red tiles: 4(n − 1); 4n − 4; or correct verbal expression
Total tiles: n^2, n x n; or correct verbal expression, such as “square the number” or “multiply by itself”
Both expressions correct with expression for red tiles in the form of total number of tiles minus number of black tiles e.g., n^2 − (n − 2)^2 or equivalent.
Expression for red tiles correct as in 20 but not expression for total tiles
Expression for total tiles correct as in 20 but not expression for red tiles
Incorrect expression including n for red tiles or total or both (includes incorrect attempts to express red tiles as difference from total tiles)
Other incorrect (including crossed out, erased, stray marks, illegible, or off task)

slope.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 1-point item with the two-parameter logistic (2PL) model, which TIMSS uses for constructed-response items worth 1 point, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1999 and 2003 eighth-grade mathematics data". What is the item's slope (discrimination) parameter a? A higher a means that the item separates students of lower and higher mathematics ability more sharply. Choose the value closest to it. The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration. Use them to place this item.

location.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 1-point item with the two-parameter logistic (2PL) model, which TIMSS uses for constructed-response items worth 1 point, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1999 and 2003 eighth-grade mathematics data". What is the item's location (difficulty) parameter b? b is on a logit scale on which the students of the calibration average about 0; a higher b means a harder item. Choose the value closest to it. The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration.
